The first sentence, "Name the explorer who reached America in 1492," is a factual historical query that stands entirely isolated from the rest of the paragraph. It introduces no thematic link to the following content.

The remaining sentences form a coherent unit focused on the evolution of media consumption. They begin with a modern adaptation of Gil Scott-Heron’s phrase to introduce the topic of streaming versus traditional television. The text then elaborates on this theme by discussing the struggle of traditional networks, the rise of streaming services, and the resulting shift in power dynamics within the entertainment industry.

In summary, while the latter four sentences work together logically to discuss the transformation of media, the initial sentence is an unrelated non-sequitur that disrupts the overall coherence of the passage.
